title: Proverbs Bible Quiz - Chapter 5
description: Ten questions on Proverbs 5: the warning against the adulteress and the call to rejoice in the wife of your youth.

questions.text: What do the lips of an adulteress drip?
questions.explanation: The lips of an adulteress drip honey, and her mouth is smoother than oil.

questions.text: What is the adulteress like in the end, in contrast with her smooth mouth?
questions.explanation: In the end she is as bitter as wormwood and as sharp as a two-edged sword.

answers.text: As cold as snow and as hard as stone
As dark as night and as deep as a pit
As bitter as wormwood and as sharp as a two-edged sword
As sour as vinegar and as sharp as a thorn

questions.text: Where do the feet of the adulteress go down to?
questions.explanation: Her feet go down to death, and her steps lead straight to Sheol.

questions.text: What are the sons told not to come near?
questions.explanation: The verse says to remove your way far from her and not to come near the door of her house.

questions.text: Who would feast on your wealth if you do not stay away from her?
questions.explanation: The warning is that strangers would feast on your wealth and your labors would enrich another man's house.

questions.text: What will the man say at his latter end, when his flesh and body are consumed?
questions.explanation: He will groan and say, "How I have hated instruction, and my heart despised reproof."

questions.text: How does the saying continue: "Drink water out of..."?
questions.explanation: The verse says to drink water out of your own cistern, running water out of your own well.

questions.text: In whom should the man rejoice?
questions.explanation: The verse says: let your spring be blessed, and rejoice in the wife of your youth.

questions.text: Before whose eyes are the ways of man?
questions.explanation: The ways of man are before Yahweh's eyes, and he examines all his paths.

questions.text: What holds the wicked man firmly?
questions.explanation: The evil deeds of the wicked ensnare him, and the cords of his sin hold him firmly.
